summary: Discovery focused on private VPC deployment options, networking constraints, and security requirements for a healthcare customer. Key topics: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, regional constraints, audit/KMS, private endpoints, egress/NAT concerns. Agreed to send topology doc and schedule POC.
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-07-14 11:00 AM PDT | Duration: 52 minutes | Attendees: Jamie Ortega, Ravi Patel (Redwood); Lena Morris, Marcus Lee, Priya Nair (Acadia)

[00:00] Jamie Ortega: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Jamie from Redwood Inference, I'm the account exec on this and with me is Ravi our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Lena Morris: Hi Jamie, hi Ravi, thanks for fitting us in. I'm Lena, CTO at Acadia, with Marcus and Priya.
[00:13] Ravi Patel: Great to meet you all. Quick agenda — understand your current infra, network/topology constraints, security controls, and timeline for private deployment.
[00:22] Marcus Lee: So to start, we're a healthcare SaaS, HIPAA-adjacent, processing PHI in some flows. We need a private deployment in our AWS account in us-east-1. Primary reqs are VPC isolation, KMS-managed keys, and auditability.
[00:36] Priya Nair: And importantly, data residency — certain patient transforms must remain in us-east-1 and not replicate to other regions. Latency sensitive endpoints for our user facing flows.
[00:47] Jamie Ortega: Totally makes sense, thanks. A couple clarifying q's: do you want Redwood to manage the control plane or do you want a self-managed private control plane in your VPC? Also, are you planning to use VPC peering, Transit Gateway, or PrivateLink for connectivity?
[01:05] Lena Morris: We prefer Redwood-managed control plane but all inference nodes must run inside our VPC. For connectivity, Marcus, what do you think? We have an existing Transit Gateway architecture across accounts.
[01:18] Marcus Lee: We'd lean toward TGW peering rather than classic VPC peering cause we have multiple accounts. Also prefer PrivateLink for any control plane endpoints but we want the data plane never to leave our VPC.
[01:33] Ravi Patel: Okay so typical pattern — Redwood provides a control plane endpoint (we can do PrivateLink or IP allowlist) and the inference fleet runs in your account in private subnets. We can support ingress via VPC endpoints and route tables so nothing traverses the public internet.
[01:47] Marcus Lee: How do you handle egress for things like image pulls or OS updates? Our security team won't allow nodes to have open internet.
[01:56] Ravi Patel: Good q. We recommend a NAT gateway in a managed egress-only subnet with explicit firewall rules. Alternatively, if you have an internal artifact repo you can host images, we support airgapped images signed by Redwood. There's also option to use an S3 VPC endpoint for pulls.
[02:15] Priya Nair: Can you support cross-region failover and still keep data in-region? We need DR in a second region but patient data can't replicate off us-east-1.
[02:25] Jamie Ortega: We can deploy standby compute in another region but configure the data plane so model weights and KV caches are stored per-region. For DR we'd typically failover compute but ensure persisted data remains in the primary region — we can discuss specifics with compliance.
[02:41] Lena Morris: On encryption — we want SSE-KMS with our customer-managed keys (CMKs). Are you able to integrate with our KMS/HSM?
[02:50] Ravi Patel: Yes, we support customer KMS integration. For Private deployments we can either use cross-account KMS grants or have keys in your account, and Redwood's nodes will use them via IAM roles. For HSM we have patterns that integrate with vendor HSMs but that's a deeper discussion.
[03:10] Marcus Lee: Audit logs — do you push operational logs to our CloudWatch or S3? We need 7 years retention for some events.
[03:17] Jamie Ortega: We can forward logs to your CloudWatch/CloudTrail and also provide an S3 sink. Our default is to send audit logs to your account; retention and lifecycle can be handled on your side.
[03:28] Priya Nair: Network specifics, do you require dedicated ENIs per node or can you use CNI overlays? We run with Cilium in our clusters.
[03:36] Ravi Patel: We usually create ENIs for the inference nodes to simplify routing; that said we have customers using CNI overlays — it's supported but we should validate MTU and other kernel params. Cilium should be fine but we'll run a short compatibility test during POC.
[03:52] Lena Morris: About PrivateLink for the control plane — how does auth happen? SSO? We use Okta and SCIM.
[04:00] Ravi Patel: Our control plane supports SAML SSO and SSO provisioning via SCIM; for PrivateLink we put an NLB in front and mTLS + token-based auth to verify connections. Okta integration is standard for our customers.
[04:16] Marcus Lee: Any hard region limitations? Some Redwood features we care about are only in specific regions.
[04:22] Jamie Ortega: Hosted models and some runtime optimizations vary by region. For Private deployments the runtime supports all major regions but specific GPU instance types availability may vary. For us-east-1 we have wide coverage; we'll confirm GPU type availability for your sizing.
[04:36] Priya Nair: Licensing and SLA — what's the typical latency SLO and do you offer SLA for private deployments?
[04:44] Jamie Ortega: For Dedicated/Private we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets depending on tier. We'll include SLA language in the enterprise contract. For latency SLOs we tune based on instance types and batching configs—you'll see benchmarks in the doc we send.
[04:59] Marcus Lee: We also need to understand fail open/fail closed behaviors. If the control plane is unreachable, do nodes keep serving?
[05:06] Ravi Patel: Yes nodes can continue serving with cached model weights and KV cache; control plane loss only affects management operations, rollouts, and config changes. We'll document exact behaviors and local fallback policies.
[05:20] Lena Morris: Ok this is helpful. Next steps — send network topology doc, security whitepaper, and proposed sizing for a 3-node cluster for POC.
[05:28] Jamie Ortega: We'll send those. Anything else from your side?
[05:31] Priya Nair: We'll send our VPC diagrams and CIDR ranges plus a list of required ports and firewall rules.
[05:37] Ravi Patel: Great. I'll also prepare a short checklist for the infra team on route tables, endpoints, and IAM roles.
[05:44] Jamie Ortega: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for the POC kickoff.

Action recap:
- Jamie: topology + security docs
- Ravi: network checklist + sizing
- Acadia: VPC diagrams + CIDRs

End of transcript.
